messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High p99 latency spike observed for /v1/generate (model: rw-13b) across eu-west-1. Autoscaler activity detected. Paging on-call.
sarah: on it. seeing p50 ok, p99 ~6s -> 15s over last 5m. throwing up dashboard now. @mike can you check runtime logs?
mike: looking. replication: around 2024-11-21T09:28:02Z we started getting an abnormal KV cache growth across pods. memory usage +30% then OOM kill on one replica. logs show continuous batching queues spiking.
sarah: that matches traces — KV cache keys exploding after recent batching change rolled to 100% at 09:25 by rolling-deploy-bot. suspect the new batching window combined with prefix caching creating many small cache entries.
lee: paging in. probable feedback loop: larger batch window -> more prefixes cached -> warming causes autoscaler to spin up -> new pods warm by filling cache -> further memory growth -> HPA scales more -> thrash.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollout-id=deploy-20241121-rolling-batching-change by @deploy-bot at 09:25:14Z. status: complete.
sarah: mitigation plan attempt 1: pause continuous batching on the model route and reduce max_batch_size to previous value. will open quick hotfix config and push canary.
mike: commands I ran to inspect pods:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=rw-13b -o wide
kubectl -n inference exec -it <pod> -- bash -c "sgxctl memstats || cat /proc/meminfo"
kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --since=15m | grep kv-cache | tail -n 50
```
logs:
```
[09:27:02] kv-cache: insert key prefix:user_msg:abcd123 size=4096 total_keys=1_200_000
[09:27:03] batching: enqueued 512 requests, window=250ms
[09:27:05] eviction: scanned 0 keys, disabled
```
sarah: I'm going to push a config override to disable prefix kv caching for this model and set batching.window_ms=80, max_batch_size=64. will do canary 10% first.
mike: make sure to add annotation to avoid autoscaler reacting to short-term CPU spikes. set hpa.stabilizationWindowSeconds=300 temporarily.
sarah: apply manifest snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rw-13b-hotfix-20241121
data:
  continuous_batching: "false"
  batching.window_ms: "80"
  batching.max_batch_size: "64"
  kv_cache.prefix_enabled: "false"
```
sarah: applied canary to two pods at 09:33. monitoring.
customer-support: any ETA on customer impact? we're seeing a few errors upstack (rate-limited/generic 503s) from two enterprise customers.
sarah: early impact: ~0.6% of requests got 503s during scale events around 09:26-09:30. Worked to reduce by draining one bad pod and restarting.
mike: after canary applied we see p99 drop to ~3s on canary pods, overall cluster p99 improving to ~6s. KV cache insert rate down by ~80% on canary.
lee: thumbs. Next step: if canary holds for 6m, roll to 30% then full. Also adjust HPA: increase minReplicas to 3 for this deployment, set cooldown to 300s, and set targetCPU to a lower steady value so it doesn't overscale on warmup.
sarah: notes for handoff: I'm going offline in ~20m. leaving monitoring checks and rollback playbook in thread. If latency climbs above 8s, flip continuous_batching back on? no, flip back OFF? wait — decision: keep continuous batching OFF until we analyze cache policy. we need longer-term change: introduce per-prefix size caps and eviction policy.
mike: creating GH issue: "kv-cache blowups w/ continuous batching" linking logs and deploy id. tagging infra/eng-runtime.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: hotfix applied (canary -> 2 pods) at 09:33:47Z. metrics: p99 improvement on canary observed by 09:36Z.
sarah: handoff to @lee for the next shift. summary for handoff:
- root cause: batching window change + prefix kv cache allowed many high-cardinality prefixes -> memory blowup -> autoscaler thrash
- mitigation taken: disabled prefix kv cache on rw-13b, reduced batch window, canary rollout, increased HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds
- impact: transient 503s ~0.6% requests during scale events, p99 from 15s -> ~4s after canary, OOM killed 1 pod restarted
- follow-ups: add per-prefix cap, eviction heuristics, require canary metrics for batching changes, regression tests for kv-cache growth
- contacts: @mike (runtime), @sarah (primary oncall), @lee (secondary)
lee: ack. I'll monitor for 2h and coordinate permanent fix with eng-runtime. also will run a synthetic traffic sweep to validate warmup behavior and autoscaler thresholds. schedule: tune HPA to use custom metric (memory+request-queue) instead of raw CPU.
customer-support: ty. I'll notify affected customers with the summary and expected mitigation timeline.
sarah: leaving notes: if you see sustained p99 >8s or more than 1% 5m errors, escalate to SEV team and page pagerduty SRE escalation.
lee: thanks all. I'll update thread with follow-up issue links and rollout plan. ending handoff at 10:01. :white_check_mark:
